chunks: “The night of al-Jumu‘ah is a radiant night, and its day is a shining day. There is no day on the face of the earth on which the sun sets with more freed from the Fire than on the day of al-Jumu‘ah. Whoever dies on the day of al-Jumu‘ah, Allah writes for him immunity from the punishment of the grave, and whoever dies on the day of al-Jumu‘ah is freed from the Fire.”

key_terms.أَزْهَرُ: Bright or shining; describing the excellence of Friday daytime.
key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: Was set free; here, freed from the Fire.
key_terms.بَرَاءَةً: Immunity or acquittal; here, protection from punishment.
key_terms.عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ: The punishment of the grave; suffering in the grave before the Hereafter.
key_terms.غَرَّاءُ: Radiant or splendid; describing the distinction of Friday night.
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْجُمُعَةِ: The night preceding Friday, described here as especially radiant and virtuous.
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, presented here as a uniquely blessed day.

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of dying on Friday in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the special virtue of the night and day of al-Jumu‘ah and highlights its distinction among all days. It also mentions divine mercy associated with this day, including freedom from the punishment of the grave and deliverance from the Fire for one who dies on it.
